label: Monday–Tuesday night: Straker picks up the knife from the dressing-table as he leaves the room (his wife's account)
quote: he had picked it up as he left the room
note: Just before he leaves the house (t.straker_leaves); the text does not order it more finely.

label: Straker's body is brought back to his villa
quote: Straker was brought back here, I presume?

label: The Inspector takes the things in Straker's pockets and puts them in a tin box
quote: I have the things themselves in the sitting-room

label: Mrs. Straker tells the police about the knife and about Derbyshire
quote: His wife tells us that the knife had lain upon the dressing-table

label: Letters for William Derbyshire are now and then addressed to Straker's house (Mrs. Straker's account)
quote: occasionally his letters were addressed here

label: Madame Lesurier makes out the milliner's account to William Derbyshire
quote: made out by Madame Lesurier, of Bond Street, to William Derbyshire
note: Before Straker's death, since the account was in his pockets; the story gives no closer date.

label: A garden-party at Plymouth "some little time ago" (Holmes's claim; Mrs. Straker denies it)
quote: Surely I met you in Plymouth at a garden-party some little time ago
note: Holmes's claim; Mrs. Straker says he is mistaken.

label: Thursday evening, a few minutes later: the landau pulls up at Straker's villa
quote: A few minutes later our driver pulled up at a neat little red-brick villa

label: Thursday evening: in the sitting-room, the Inspector lays out Straker's things
quote: We all filed into the front room and sat round the central table

label: Thursday evening: Mrs. Straker meets them in the passage as they leave the sitting-room
quote: As we emerged from the sitting-room a woman, who had been waiting in the passage
